skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate AI videos with the RunComfy CLI. The skill routes text-to-video, image-to-video, and video extension requests to suitable RunComfy video models.
skill.summary: Route AI video requests to RunComfy models with prompt guidance and CLI commands.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, catalog URLs, example media URLs, and model-selection wording. No prompt injection attempt, hidden command execution, credential exfiltration, or malicious network callback was found in SKILL.md. The skill intentionally uses the RunComfy CLI and includes reasonable security guidance for token handling, user-provided references, and endpoint scope.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger noisy static detections.
remediation.suggestion: Keep install commands clearly marked as operator setup and keep runtime instructions scoped to runcomfy commands.

remediation.issue: Reference asset URLs can influence generated media.
remediation.suggestion: Continue instructing agents to use only user-provided image, audio, and video URLs for the current task.

content.value_statement: Choosing the right video model and prompt format can slow production work. This skill selects a RunComfy route and prepares clear CLI-ready generation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Selects RunComfy models for text-to-video, image-to-video, and video extension tasks.
Provides prompt guidance for HappyHorse, Wan, Seedance, Kling, Veo, Hailuo, and Dreamina models.
Shows RunComfy CLI invocation patterns using model endpoints, input fields, and output directories.
Recommends routes for social clips, product spins, cinematic ads, character narratives, and lip-sync scenes.
Explains token handling, endpoint boundaries, output downloads, and reference asset risks.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy account or token.
Model availability, pricing, duration limits, and schemas can change on RunComfy.
Generated video quality depends on the model, prompt, references, and source media.
The skill does not edit videos locally or provide custom model training.

use_cases.title: Create Short Social Clips
use_cases.description: Generate vertical or square clips with a suitable model, duration, aspect ratio, and audio direction.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Images
use_cases.description: Turn product stills into controlled motion clips such as rotations, hero shots, or simple reveal scenes.

use_cases.title: Plan Cinematic Video Concepts
use_cases.description: Choose higher quality models and prompt language for camera movement, lens style, references, and shot pacing.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Text-to-Video Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with only a scene idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a short text-to-video clip of [subject] doing [main action] in [setting]. Choose the best RunComfy model, suggest duration and aspect ratio, and provide the RunComfy command.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Still Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate image-to-video request using a reference image URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this image: [image URL]. The subject should [motion], the camera should [camera behavior], and the scene should feel [style]. Pick the best RunComfy image-to-video model.

prompt_templates.title: Model Match for Production Goal
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison across quality, speed, audio, and realism needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a video for [goal] with [constraints]. Compare the best RunComfy routes for quality, speed, audio support, and realism. Recommend one final model and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Reference Cinematic Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt using subject, scene, audio, or video references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a cinematic RunComfy generation plan using these references: [reference list]. Preserve [identity or product detail], use [camera language], and produce a prompt for [duration and aspect ratio].

output_examples.input: A user asks for a vertical launch teaser with a product photo and subtle motion.
output: Recommended route: image-to-video with a model suited for product motion.
Prompt direction: keep the product stable, add a slow rotation, and avoid extra background movement.
Delivery guidance: use a vertical aspect ratio and save results to a dedicated output folder.

output_examples.input: A user wants a talking character synced to a voiceover file.
output: Recommended route: a lip-sync capable text-to-video model with an audio URL field.
Prompt direction: describe the speaker and scene while allowing the audio to drive mouth movement.
Safety note: use only the voiceover URL that the user provided for this task.

output_examples.input: A user needs a cinematic concept clip with several visual references.
output: Recommended route: a multi-modal cinematic model that accepts reference assets.
Prompt direction: assign each reference a clear role, such as subject, mood, or motion.
Review guidance: generate a fast draft before spending on a higher quality final render.

best_practices: Choose the route from the desired outcome before writing model-specific prompts.
Use explicit motion, camera, duration, and aspect-ratio instructions for every generation.
Use only user-provided reference URLs and keep RunComfy tokens out of prompts and logs.
anti_patterns: Do not use a high-cost model for simple drafts before testing cheaper routes.
Do not paste private tokens, unpublished assets, or sensitive voice files into prompts.
Do not ask for precise physical motion without choosing a model that supports realism well.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It prepares and runs RunComfy CLI workflows that use RunComfy model endpoints.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it turn an image into a video?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video routes for several RunComfy models.

faq.question: Can it help with lip-sync videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends a model route that accepts an audio URL for dialog-driven lip-sync.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI and sign in, or provide a RunComfy token through the environment.

faq.question: Does it protect private assets?
faq.answer: It reminds users to provide only task-specific reference URLs and to avoid exposing tokens.
